Born: July 6, 1907, 8:30 AM local time, Coyoacán, Mexico. Source: Astro-Databank, Rodden rating AA.

The AA rating means the birth time comes from a reliable record, so the rising sign, the Midheaven and the houses below can be read at face value. Open Frida Kahlo's chart on Astrolas to follow the wheel while you read.

Three planets sit together in one sign and one house. The Sun, Jupiter and Neptune all fall in Cancer, and all three land in the 11th house, the part of the chart the Astrolas library ties to friendship, groups and shared ideals. That is an unusual amount of weight on one placement, and it points toward a life built as much through a circle of fellow artists and causes as through solitary work at an easel.

muc.ten: Sun, Jupiter and Neptune in Cancer, all in the 11th house
doan: In order: Neptune at 12°24', the Sun at 13°23' and Jupiter at 20°26', all Cancer, all in the 11th house. The Sun and Neptune sit close enough to form a conjunction, orb 0°59'.

The library reads the Cancer Sun as sensitive, intuitive, and guided by a deep need for security, family and lasting connection, with a tendency to retreat behind a shell when hurt. Sun in the 11th house adds a strong pull toward friendship and group causes, often a willingness to lead or contribute to organizations and shared projects, valuing purpose over personal recognition. Kahlo spent her life inside a tight circle of painters, writers and political allies in Mexico City, and much of her later recognition came through those same networks rather than through a solo path.

Sun conjunct Neptune, in the library's reading, describes a dreamer and a poet, creative and intuitive enough to inspire others, with a rich imagination and a gift for the arts. The caution it names is a pull away from plain reality, toward idealizing what is wished for over what is actually there. Neptune in Cancer reads as strong intuition tied to home and family, with the house, the chart's own sanctuary, as a place of rest; on a generational level, this placement marks a cohort living through upheaval in family structures. Jupiter in Cancer, one of its most fortunate placements by the library's own account, favors real estate, inheritance and steady accumulation, with family as the emotional base. Kahlo spent most of her life in the Coyoacán house where she had grown up, later known as the Casa Azul, now the museum that holds her work.

muc.ten: Mars conjunct Uranus in Capricorn, house 5
doan: Mars sits at 13°24' Capricorn, retrograde, and Uranus at 10°37' Capricorn, also retrograde, both in the 5th house, the library's house of creative work and romance. The two form a conjunction, orb 2°47'.

The library reads this Mars as energy held back and released only when it truly matters, built on willpower, endurance and a drive toward status and financial security through disciplined, practical work. Uranus in Capricorn adds a steadfast will aimed at reform, a wish to shape direction rather than be shaped by it, generational for her entire cohort but personal here through house and conjunction. Mars conjunct Uranus, in the library's reading, is determination paired with a rebellious streak and a refusal to be bound to any set pattern, the kind of placement that seizes a sudden opportunity and turns it into a genuine turning point in life, though it warns of hasty action and the risk of accidents along the way.

In 1925, a bus accident changed the direction of Kahlo's life. She began painting seriously during the long recovery that followed, a sudden and unplanned turn that reads very much like the library's description of this exact pairing. The 5th house adds creative work and romance in the same breath: her marriage to the muralist Diego Rivera, in 1929, bound her art and her private life together for the rest of her career.

muc.ten: Venus conjunct Pluto in Gemini, between the 10th and 11th houses
doan: Venus sits at 24°20' Gemini, in the 11th house, and Pluto at 23°45' Gemini, in the 10th house. The two form the tightest aspect with library text anywhere in this chart, a conjunction at orb 0°35'.

The library's Venus in Gemini wants a partner who is also a conversation, someone who keeps the mind as engaged as the heart, and it names a wide social circle as part of that need. Venus in the 11th house adds that romance itself can begin inside a friendship or a shared artistic group. Pluto in Gemini is generational, tied by the library to a cohort living through a revolution in communication and technology, and personal here through the 10th house of career, where it reads as a drive to reach the top of one's field through repeated cycles of reinvention. Venus conjunct Pluto describes a magnetism carrying an edge of power and mystery, drawing both money and admiration, alongside real artistic and financial ability. Its shadow, in the library's own words, is possessiveness, jealousy and a love that can come to dominate much of a life.

Kahlo met Rivera inside the same political and artistic circles that Venus in the 11th house describes, and their marriage became one of the most famous and most turbulent partnerships in twentieth-century art: they divorced in 1939 and remarried in 1940. The Louvre had bought one of her paintings in 1939, making her the first twentieth-century Mexican artist in its collection.

The Moon sits at 29°43' Taurus, the final degree of the sign, in the 10th house. The library's Taurus Moon is steady, resistant to sudden change, and finds security in familiar surroundings, often keeping objects and heirlooms that carry sentimental weight. The Moon in the 10th house ties emotional security to public standing and the esteem of others, with the library noting that a parent, often the mother, tends to be a steady source of encouragement.

Kahlo's home, the Casa Azul, was kept full of folk art and personal objects, exactly the kind of comfort through belongings the library assigns to this Moon. Her father worked as a photographer in Mexico City, and she painted for most of her life from the house she had grown up in.

Saturn sits at 27°27' Pisces, in the 8th house. The library reads Saturn in Pisces as a placement rich in intuition and imagination but light on an easy path to material success, one that teaches its lessons through hard situations faced rather than avoided, often leading toward meaning found in philosophy, literature or spiritual tradition. Saturn in the 8th house adds caution around shared money and inheritance, with results that tend to arrive slowly.

Her paintings drew heavily on Mexican religious folk art, including the retablo tradition of small devotional paintings, a visual language close to the library's note about meaning built through spiritual and symbolic material.

muc.ten: Leo rising, and Mercury in Leo
doan: The Ascendant sits at 23°30' Leo. The Astrolas library has no entry for Leo rising on its own. Two aspects to it carry no text yet either: Pluto sextile the Ascendant, orb 0°14', and Venus sextile the Ascendant, orb 0°50', both tying the Gemini pair back to the chart's face.

Mercury sits at 6°20' Leo, in the 12th house. The library's Mercury in Leo is confident, expressive, drawn to public speaking and performance, with a dramatic style that enjoys being watched, though it can turn stubborn when challenged. In the 12th house, that same expressiveness folds inward: a mind that shares little of its private world, trusted with other people's secrets, and most comfortable working things out alone before showing the result. Kahlo was known for a distinctive personal style, Tehuana dress and bold jewelry, paired with a body of work, many of its paintings self-portraits, that let her control exactly how much of her inner life reached the outside.

The tightest single contact in the whole chart has no library text at all: the Sun in Cancer is almost exactly opposite Mars in Capricorn, orb 0°01'. Read through the two placements alone, it sets the chart's friendship-and-family side directly across from its private, disciplined drive.

muc.ten: What the chart adds up to
doan: The chart does not explain where the talent came from. What it shows is a structure: warmth and belonging concentrated in Cancer and the 11th house, set against a Capricorn, Taurus and Pisces current running through houses 5, 8 and 10 that favors discipline, memory and quiet transformation over an easy public path. Kahlo died in 1954, at the Coyoacán house where she was born.

The Cancer group in the 11th house: the Sun, Jupiter and Neptune together, with the Sun and Neptune close enough to form a conjunction. It lines up with a life lived inside a close circle of artists and causes.
